reference.title: Dose-Dependent Impact of Metformin on Osteoblast-Specific Biomarkers in Cultured Rat Primary Osteoblasts

before_text.13: A metallic implant in the rat atlantoaxial joint produces misalignment and blood-pressure elevation [1]. Oxidative stress is implicated in hypertension [2]; the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM) regulates blood pressure [3], and experimental studies link regional redox disturbances to cardiovascular regulation [4,5]. We examined regional biochemical indices and exploratory Nox1/Nox4-targeted RT-qPCR estimates. Blood-pressure observations were shared with a related Ang II/AT1-R report [6], whereas the present biochemical and targeted RT-qPCR observations were not reported there.
before_text.19: Across the terminal cohorts, Welch ANOVA gave F(2, 9.816) = 91.626 for SOD, F(2, 8.500) = 130.738 for MDA and F(2, 7.804) = 314.907 for fluorescence (all P < 0.001). In week-4 model versus sham records, SOD was 0.564 ± 0.072 versus 1.122 ± 0.072 U/mg protein, MDA 0.349 ± 0.034 versus 0.095 ± 0.017 nmol/mg protein, and fluorescence 3295.6 ± 216.3 versus 1326.9 ± 50.6 AU (Fig. 1; all Games–Howell-adjusted P < 0.001; Supplementary Table S1). Normalized Nox1-targeted assay estimates were 1.459 ± 0.156 versus 1.000 ± 0.134, and Nox4-targeted estimates 2.902 ± 0.558 versus 1.000 ± 0.233 (Fig. 2; Holm-adjusted P = 0.0037 and 0.0001).
before_text.20: At the later restoration endpoint, SOD was 1.035 ± 0.101, MDA 0.213 ± 0.049 and fluorescence 2265.6 ± 131.6 in the same respective units; all differed from model values (adjusted P < 0.001). Relative to sham, MDA and fluorescence remained higher (P = 0.0033 and <0.001), whereas the SOD difference was nonsignificant (P = 0.2534). Restoration Nox1/Nox4-targeted estimates were 1.180 ± 0.090/1.645 ± 0.227, lower than model values (adjusted P = 0.0139/0.0037). Compared with sham, the Nox4-targeted estimate remained higher (P = 0.0099); the Nox1-targeted difference was nonsignificant (P = 0.0618). Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence or normalization. Full three-cohort statistics are supplied.
before_text.22: Regional sampling and missing identity-linked records limit anatomical attribution and verification of biological replication. Later restoration observations confound implant removal with age, elapsed time, recovery and repeat anesthesia/surgery; common model origin does not remove this confounding. Omission of postoperative analgesia raises unresolved animal-welfare and pain/stress concerns. Disclosure cannot retrospectively establish that the procedures matched an approved protocol or that withholding analgesia was authorized. Small exploratory samples and male-only inclusion limit precision and generalizability. Same-time SOD/MDA observations deserve emphasis; causal or gene-expression conclusions require validated assays, traceable samples and time-matched controls.
